title: Twitch Defaults to Using Streamer Content to Train Amazon's AI Model, Causing Strong Discontent in the Community
excerpt: Twitch, the live streaming platform, recently announced that it will start using creators' live stream content to help train generative AI models for its parent
content_html:
Twitch, the live streaming platform, recently announced that it will start using creators' live stream content to help train generative AI models for its parent company Amazon. This move has sparked strong resistance within the Twitch creator community, with the focus being on the policy's "opt-in by default" mechanism, which means streamers need to manually opt out without being aware in order to avoid their audio and video content being used to train AI.

During a live event on the official channel, Twitch Community Manager Mary Kish and Chief Product Officer Mike Minton faced questions from nearly 3,000 viewers. In response to the overwhelming number of messages asking "Why not make it opt-out by default?" Minton bluntly replied that if it were set as "opt-out by default," no one would be willing to participate voluntarily.

Twitch management admitted that the platform is well aware of the general opposition among streamers toward generative AI, as most AI products are trained using publicly available data from the internet without the creators' consent. Because of this, when announcing this news, the platform deliberately framed it as an "optional setting to opt out of Amazon's company-wide AI model training," which caused many streamers to worry and get confused about whether their content had already been secretly collected.

Kish added that allowing users to opt out was meant to align with the community's firm rejection of helping train AI. Similar to other tech giants that directly use public platform data for AI training, although Twitch provides an opt-out option, this move once again highlights the deep conflict between the platform and creators over AI copyright and data usage rights.

For streamers who wish to refuse participation, they can currently find the "Generative AI Training" option by scrolling down to the "Safety & Privacy" tab in their channel settings (not the Creator Dashboard) and manually turn it off.

content_html_zh:
直播平台 Twitch 最近宣布将开始使用创作者的直播内容来帮助其母公司亚马逊训练生成人工智能模型。 此举在 Twitch 创作者社区内引发了强烈抵制，焦点在于该政策的“默认选择加入”机制，这意味着主播需要在不知情的情况下手动选择退出，以避免自己的音频和视频内容被用来训练 AI。

在官方频道的现场活动中，Twitch 社区经理 Mary Kish 和首席产品官 Mike Minton 面临着近 3,000 名观众的提问。 回应大量询问“为什么不默认选择退出？”的消息。 明顿直言，如果设定为“默认退出”，没有人愿意自愿参与。

Twitch 管理层承认，该平台很清楚主播对生成式人工智能的普遍反对，因为大多数人工智能产品都是在未经创作者同意的情况下使用互联网上的公开数据进行训练的。 正因为如此，该平台在宣布这一消息时，故意将其描述为“选择退出亚马逊全公司人工智能模型训练的可选设置”，这让许多主播担心和困惑，他们的内容是否已经被秘密收集。

Kish 补充说，允许用户选择退出是为了与社区坚决拒绝帮助训练人工智能保持一致。 与其他直接使用公共平台数据进行AI训练的科技巨头类似，尽管Twitch提供了退出选项，但此举再次凸显了平台与创作者之间在AI版权和数据使用权方面的深刻冲突。

对于希望拒绝参与的主播，他们目前可以通过向下滚动到频道设置（而不是创作者仪表板）中的“安全和隐私”选项卡来找到“生成人工智能训练”选项，然后手动将其关闭。
